evidence: Every interactive, time-varying and viewport behaviour the brief asks for is graded through an explicit action, not a first paint. VIEWPORT: ui.md:17 requires usability at about 390 px; tests/scored/polish/judge.toml:68 (cw_narrow_width_usable) says 'Resize the browser viewport to about 390 by 844 pixels and reload', then scroll vertically to five areas, type in the editor, press Run, and 'Restore the desktop viewport afterwards'. WAITS: tests/scored/functional/prompt.md:25 'Where waiting is required, wait the stated time; do not shorten it'; functional/judge.toml:281 (wait until run finished, then at least eight more seconds, then click preview buttons), :299 (time-limit reason within about ten seconds), :308 and :317 (act immediately, then 'wait at least eight more seconds', each with a control proving the delayed write happens and a void-attempt rule), :380 and :398 (watch tab A for up to ten seconds without acting in it). INTERACTION: all 42 functional criteria prescribe real keys, mouse clicks, drags and modifier-clicks (functional/prompt.md:20; app_context.md:18-19); the render gate itself types and reloads (gates/render/judge.toml:23). STATE TOGGLES: polish/judge.toml:50 (Undo/Redo availability at three points), :59 (unsaved marker on edit, Undo, Save), :23 (keyboard traversal with visible focus), :41 (focus return after five actions). VISUAL: visual/prompt.md:11-12 fixes a 1440x900 viewport and tells the judge to enter a ten-line draft, Run once, click into the code, double-click a word and 'watch the caret for about two seconds, because a caret may blink' before screenshots, which matches visual/judge.toml:24 grading caret and selection visibility; the golden caret does blink (style.css:19-21, 1s step-end). THEMING: not applicable; the brief asks for no theme, the golden pins data-theme to dark (app.tsx:120) and offers no toggle, and no criterion grades a theme. The task dropped the template's 390 px visual review and theme review lines; that is consistent because no visual criterion grades responsiveness (visual/prompt.md:19 sends narrow-screen behaviour to polish). Weak-app test: an app that looks fine at first paint but overflows at 390 px, drops a pending timer late, or never updates an idle tab fails the cited criteria; a conforming alternative with a blinking or canvas-drawn caret is not penalised (app_context.md:28). Run evidence: the scripted golden run on these bytes resizes with setViewportSize 390x844 and restores 1440x900 (polish.cjs:105,124; results/polish.json cw_narrow_width_usable true), but that is a script, not the judge. The hosted configured-judge run was on an EARLIER candidate; its reasoning shows the judge resizing ('Viewport resized to 390x844 and reloaded: scrollWidth 390 = clientWidth 390'), waiting ('9s after a run finished, clicking the preview's One button produced DELAYED-MARKER ~1s later') and observing an idle tab ('appear in A's library within ~6s without reload'). The narrow-width criterion wording has changed since that run. No configured judge run exists for these bytes, so risk stays true and the run verdict is NOT EXERCISED.
